newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker amid sloppy auction.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker amid sloppy auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in light trade on Wednesday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, as supply pressures weighed on the market following a 10-year government bond auction, analysts said.

"It's been another one of those fairly quiet days. There was a lack of activity," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities. "The 10-year auction was a little bit sloppy. It wasn't a disaster."
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 fell C$0.35 to C$101.40 to yield 7.872 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 1/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 85 basis points from 82 points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
"There was bit of (spread) unwinding, but I would say it's more supply pressures," said Harvinder Kalirai, Canadian analyst with New York-based financial analysis firm I.D.E.A.

The Government of Canada today auctioned C$2.4 billion of 7.25 percent bonds maturing on June 1, 2007. The average yield was 7.458 percent, with a low of 7.452 percent and a high of 7.465 percent. The allotment ratio at the high accepted yield was 31.75182 percent.

"Recent market insecurity led to a sloppy Canada 10-year auction Wednesday. The absence of many of the ususal account buyers suggests that interest in Canada is deteriorating," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analysts for Technical Data, in a commentary.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.22 to C$97.18 to yield 7.397 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 1/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 57 basis points from 53 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.84 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.26 percent.
